analysis.title: Not Out of The Fight Yet... CRWV Delivers a $133B Backlog & Double-Digit OMs
key_insights: Loop reiterates BUY and $155 price target on CoreWeave (CRWV, $48.73) after Q3 FY2026 results. Q3 revenue was $3.7B (+168% YoY, more than $1B added sequentially), above the high end of guidance.
Adjusted operating income was $379M, a 10% operating margin, up from 5% in Q2 and 1% in Q1. Adjusted EBITDA was $2.3B (+169% YoY) at a 62% margin.

Revenue backlog ended Q3 at $133B (+138% YoY). Over 50% of it is tied to contracts where customer delivery is expected to start by the end of 2026. Management cited 10x more qualified demand than available capacity through 2027.

Active power reached 1.7 GW (more than 850 MW added year-to-date), with line of sight to more than 1.85 GW by year-end 2026. International expansion accounts for 1.3 GW of contracted power outside the US.

More than 300,000 GPUs come off their initial contracts across 2027 and 2028 (over 130,000 in 2027, about 170,000 in 2028). The hardware is paid off and owned outright. Renewals at current pricing add approaching $4B of annualized revenue from the 2027 fleet and nearly $10B including 2028, with no additional hardware CapEx.
Pricing for legacy Ampere and Hopper GPUs rose 30% to 50% QoQ. CoreWeave raised pricing across SKUs by about 25% in July and another 10% later in Q3, and pricing continues to rise in Q4.

Short-term capacity commands more than $40M per megawatt annually versus $20M to $25M for standard four- to five-year contracts. CoreWeave says this lets it recoup hardware CapEx within 6 to 18 months.

FY2026 revenue guidance was raised to $13.0B-$13.3B (from $11.7B-$12.1B). Adjusted operating income guidance is $1.275B-$1.375B and CapEx is tightened to $37B-$39B. Exit-2026 ARR is guided to $20B-$21B.
Adjusted net loss is expected to narrow meaningfully in 2027, with positive adjusted net income in the first half of 2028.

CoreWeave expects about $9B in cash prepayments and deposits over the next three months, with more than $3B tied to already paid-off infrastructure. Management will not use the unsecured debt market at current yields and plans to rely on asset-level delayed draw term loans, prepayments and OEM financing. It expects to raise less than $5B of incremental parent-level capital through 2027.
Q3 operating cash flow was $2.0B. CapEx was $14.5B as deliveries were pulled forward from Q4.

CoreWeave Omni lets customers run workloads on CoreWeave software while owning the underlying infrastructure, a capital-light growth path. More than half of new customers this year came from outside tech and AI labs, 10% of Fortune 500 companies are customers, and 70% of new cloud customers in Q3 use Forge.
Loop's FY2026E revenue is $13,326M versus consensus $12,825M, and FY2027E is $29,099M versus consensus $26,477M. FY2027E EBITDA is $18,005M versus consensus $16,686M.
The $155 target is based on 10x EV/EBITDA on Loop's FY2027 estimates.

market_movers.rationale: Q3 revenue and margins beat, backlog reached $133B, and FY26 guidance was raised. Paid-off GPUs rolling off contract add up to $10B of annualized revenue without new CapEx.

earnings_insights: CRWV Q3 FY2026 reported revenue $3.7B (+168% YoY), above the high end of company guidance. Reported 11/10-11/11.

CRWV Q3 adjusted operating income $379M (10% margin), adjusted EBITDA $2.3B (62% margin). Q3 revenue was $3,661M vs Loop Q3 2027E comparison not applicable. The report gives no Q3 2026 consensus revenue figure.
CRWV Q3 GAAP EPS per Loop's table was -$0.95 (loss from continuing operations -$529M).
CRWV FY2026 guidance raised: revenue $13.0B-$13.3B (prior $11.7B-$12.1B), adjusted operating income $1.275B-$1.375B, CapEx $37B-$39B.
Loop FY2026E revenue $13,326M vs consensus est $12,825M. Loop FY2026E EBITDA $8,357M vs consensus est $7,494M. Loop Q4 2026E revenue $5,012M vs consensus est $4,692M.
Loop FY2027E revenue $29,099M vs consensus est $26,477M. Loop FY2027E EBITDA $18,005M vs consensus est $16,686M.
risk_factors: Customer concentration: one customer is 71% of revenue, and the backlog is driven mainly by OpenAI. Customers may seek alternatives with more current capacity (for example Microsoft's deal with Nebius).
Investor concentration: Magnetar holds about 25% and is trying to sell.

TAM risk: if hyperscalers decide the AI compute market is smaller than forecast and cut spending, the report says the impact on neoclouds would be catastrophic, forcing price competition, lower estimates and harder financing.
Competition from AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Crusoe, Lambda and Nebius, and from custom silicon (Google TPUs, Amazon Trainium/Inferentia).
Power and real estate constraints despite 3.1 GW of contracted power.
Regulatory changes on AI development, data privacy and energy consumption.
Technology obsolescence from NVDA's 12-month GPU release cycle and the CapEx it requires.
Financing risk: the business is capital-intensive and depends on debt and equity markets, with 88% debt to capitalization.
vol_and_positioning: Magnetar owns roughly 25% of CRWV shares and has been trying to sell part of its position since its lock-up ended after the June-quarter results. The lock-up expiry was also a short-selling catalyst for some investors.
geopolitical: The report notes that the recent elections could complicate bringing capacity online, which would raise the value of short-term capacity premiums.
